prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

The invention relates to a portable device for video electroencephalography. The device has a central portion to which a plurality of arcuate arms are directly or indirectly connected in a movable manner. The arms together define a helmet structure adapted to be worn on the head of a patient, arm is configured to allow mounting of one or more electrodes which are connected to an electronic central unit mounted on the helmet structure. The device also has a supporting member and a video camera mounted on the supporting member so as to face the helmet structure, said video camera. The arms have a first arm and a second arm which extend away from each other in a longitudinal direction (L), as well as a third arm and a fourth arm which extend away from each other in a front direction (F). The first and second arms are pivoted on the central portion about respective axes parallel to the front direction (F), and the third and fourth arms are pivoted about respective axes parallel to the longitudinal direction (L).

outputs.L1:
The invention relates to a portable video electroencephalography device. The device comprises a central portion to which a plurality of arcuate arms are movably connected, either directly or indirectly. Together, the arms define a helmet structure adapted to be worn on a patient’s head. Each arm is configured to accommodate one or more electrodes connected to an electronic central unit mounted on the helmet structure.

The device further comprises a supporting member and a video camera mounted on the supporting member so as to face the helmet structure. The plurality of arms includes first and second arms extending away from each other in a longitudinal direction (L), as well as third and fourth arms extending away from each other in a front direction (F). The first and second arms are pivotally connected to the central portion about respective axes parallel to the front direction (F), while the third and fourth arms are pivotally connected about respective axes parallel to the longitudinal direction (L).

The invention concerns a portable video-electroencephalography apparatus. It includes a central section carrying multiple curved arms, each coupled either directly or through an intermediate component so that it can move. Collectively, the arms form a helmet-shaped assembly designed to fit on a patient’s head. Each arm can support one or more electrodes connected to an electronic central unit installed on the helmet assembly.

outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a portable device designed for performing video electroencephalography (video EEG). The device includes a central portion movably connected to a plurality of arcuate arms that collectively form a helmet structure configured to be worn on a patient’s head. Each arcuate arm is capable of supporting one or more electrodes, which are electrically connected to an electronic central unit mounted on the helmet. This arrangement enables the acquisition and processing of electroencephalographic signals while maintaining a compact and portable configuration.

The device further includes a video camera mounted on a supporting member and oriented toward the helmet structure. The camera is positioned to record the patient during EEG monitoring, thereby allowing the recorded video to be synchronized or otherwise correlated with the acquired electroencephalographic data.

The plurality of arcuate arms includes first and second arms extending substantially in a longitudinal direction and configured to pivot about respective axes oriented in a front direction. Third and fourth arms extend substantially in the front direction and are configured to pivot about respective axes oriented in a longitudinal direction. The movable connections between the central portion and the arms permit the helmet structure to be adjusted to accommodate different head shapes and sizes while maintaining appropriate positioning of the electrodes.
outputs.L4:
A portable video electroencephalography device is configured to acquire electroencephalographic signals from a patient while simultaneously recording video of the patient. The device includes a helmet-like supporting structure that can be positioned on the patient’s head. A plurality of movable, generally arcuate arms are arranged around the structure, with each arm carrying one or more electrodes for contacting selected regions of the scalp.

The arms are arranged in opposed pairs and are pivotably connected to the helmet structure. At least some of the arms pivot about a substantially longitudinal axis extending from the front toward the rear of the patient’s head, while other arms pivot about a substantially frontal or transverse axis. This multi-axis movement allows the electrodes to be repositioned to accommodate different head shapes and sizes and to establish contact at desired measurement locations. The arms may be adjusted independently so that adequate electrode pressure and signal quality can be maintained without requiring a rigid, patient-specific helmet.

An electronic unit is mounted on or integrated into the helmet structure. The electronic unit receives signals from the electrodes and may amplify, filter, digitize, process, store, or transmit the acquired EEG data. Locating the electronic unit on the helmet reduces the length and number of external leads, improves portability, and permits the patient to move more freely during monitoring.

The device further includes a supporting member extending from the helmet structure. A camera is mounted on the supporting member and oriented toward the patient, particularly the patient’s face and upper body. Because the camera moves with the helmet, it can maintain a useful view of the patient while EEG signals are being recorded. The camera data and EEG data may be synchronized so that observable movements, behavioral events, or clinical episodes can be correlated with corresponding electrical activity in the brain.

In use, the helmet-like structure is placed on the patient’s head, the arcuate arms are pivoted to position the electrodes against the scalp, and the camera is adjusted to frame the patient. The electronic unit then records or transmits the EEG signals together with the associated video. The combination of adjustable electrode supports, helmet-mounted electronics, and an integrated patient-facing camera provides a compact and portable system for video-EEG monitoring in clinical, ambulatory, emergency, or remote-care environments.

**The Power of “The”**

“The” is one of the smallest yet most important words in the English language. Known as the definite article, it points to a specific person, place, object, or idea. When we say “the book,” we refer to a particular book that the listener is expected to recognize.

Despite its simplicity, “the” gives language clarity and precision. It helps transform general concepts into familiar or unique ones, such as “the sun,” “the world,” or “the future.” This modest word demonstrates how even the smallest elements of language can carry significant meaning.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the key features of a patent invention for a portable video electroencephalography device, including the helmet arms, electrodes, central electronic unit, support member, camera, and pivot-axis orientations.
counterfactuals.output:
The invention is a self-contained, portable video-EEG headset with these principal features:

- **Helmet arms:** Multiple curved arms extend around the wearer’s head and can pivot to accommodate different head sizes and shapes.
- **Electrodes:** EEG electrodes are mounted along the arms and held against selected scalp locations, allowing multichannel brain-signal acquisition without a conventional wired cap.
- **Central electronic unit:** A housing on the helmet mechanically supports the arms and contains the EEG acquisition, processing, storage, power, and/or communication electronics, reducing external cabling.
- **Support member:** A movable support or boom is connected to the central unit and positions imaging equipment relative to the wearer.
- **Camera:** A video camera on the support records the wearer—especially the face and body—so visible behavior can be synchronized with the EEG data.
- **Pivot-axis arrangement:** The helmet arms pivot about axes generally oriented in the front-to-back direction of the head, permitting inward and outward adjustment. The camera-support assembly pivots about a generally side-to-side axis, substantially transverse or perpendicular to the arm-pivot axes, so the camera can move between a usable viewing position and a compact/stowed position.

Together, these elements provide synchronized EEG and video monitoring in a compact, wearable system suitable for portable or ambulatory use.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract describing a wearable video EEG apparatus with four movable arcuate arms extending in longitudinal and front directions.
counterfactuals.output: A wearable video electroencephalography (EEG) apparatus includes a head-mountable support structure, an EEG acquisition module, and an imaging device configured to capture video of a wearer during EEG monitoring. Four movable arcuate arms extend from the support structure, including arms extending generally in a longitudinal direction and arms extending generally in a front direction. Each arcuate arm is independently adjustable relative to the support structure to conform to the wearer’s head and carries one or more electrodes positionable against selected scalp locations. The arms may translate, pivot, flex, or lock in position to maintain electrode contact while accommodating different head sizes and shapes. The EEG acquisition module receives signals from the electrodes and temporally associates the signals with video obtained by the imaging device. A controller, power source, memory, and wireless communication interface may be incorporated into the support structure to enable untethered, synchronized recording and transmission of video and EEG data.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Explain the construction of a portable video-EEG helmet whose adjustable arms carry electrodes and pivot around a central portion, with a camera facing the patient.
counterfactuals.output:
A portable video‑EEG helmet can be constructed as a lightweight head-mounted frame with four main subsystems:

1. **Central support portion**
   - A rigid or semi-rigid central section rests over the crown of the patient’s head.
   - It serves as the structural hub and may house the EEG amplifier, battery, processor, wireless transmitter, and arm-locking mechanisms.
   - Padding and adjustable straps stabilize the helmet without relying on the electrodes for support.

2. **Pivoting electrode arms**
   - Several curved or articulated arms attach to the central portion through hinges or rotary joints.
   - The arms pivot radially around the hub so that the helmet can accommodate different head sizes and shapes.
   - Detents, friction hinges, clamps, or locking screws hold each arm at the selected angle.
   - Each arm carries one or more spring-loaded, flexible, or sliding electrode mounts. These allow the electrodes to contact the scalp despite variations in hair thickness and head contour.
   - Conductors from the electrodes run through or along the arms to the EEG electronics in the central portion. Arms may be removable for cleaning or electrode-layout changes.

3. **Patient-facing camera assembly**
   - A forward-extending bracket supports a compact camera directed back toward the patient’s face and upper body.
   - The bracket is positioned outside the normal field of view while keeping the face in frame as the patient moves.
   - A wide-angle lens and optional infrared illumination permit recording in dim conditions.
   - Because the camera moves with the helmet, it maintains a relatively constant view of the patient, helping synchronize visible behavior with EEG activity.

4. **Recording and portability features**
   - EEG and video streams share timestamps or are recorded by a common controller, allowing clinical events to be correlated with electrical activity.
   - Data may be stored locally or transmitted wirelessly to a monitoring station.
   - A rechargeable battery, compact electronics, cable strain relief, ventilation, washable pads, and rounded lightweight components make the unit portable and wearable.

In use, the helmet is placed on the head, the arms are pivoted until the electrodes align with the desired scalp locations, and the individual electrode mounts are adjusted to obtain reliable contact. The arms are then locked, the camera angle is set, and synchronized video‑EEG recording begins. Any clinical version would need appropriate electrical isolation, biocompatible materials, cleaning provisions, and medical-device validation.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3
